evidence: Accelerated, binding-order structural campaigns with explicit raw throughput, ramp, budgets, plant capital and buyer advances. No actual contracts, cost advantage, engineering capacity or commissioning schedule established.
boundaries: All structural modules are assumed qualified and delivered at the source cost model price. Dense or nested components are delivered; giant fragile systems are assembled at their destination.

Eligible orders are the existing 15 Gt structural subset, with no further 15 Gt on top as an additional programme. Raw nameplate, power and route capacity scale together from the source 100 Mt/year plant. Refining chemistry, manufacturing design and expansion lead time remain unqualified.

A binding customer contract and annual budget are assumed. Additional one-time buyer advances require extra buyer funds and create delivery liabilities; they are financing, not sales or GDP at receipt.

Output is capped by ramp, budget, route, power, local feed and the finite order. The campaign ends when all orders are served or the chosen horizon ends; a horizon is not an atmospheric shutdown rule.

The manufacturing cost share and capital allowance are inherited scenario calibrations. Initial capital, replacement, fixed costs, decommissioning and terminal recovery are all counted; no operating cash is called profit after capital without that reconciliation.

All buyer payments are programme funded by default. An alternative external-buyer interpretation requires independently financed, otherwise identical orders; a buyer advance does not change that provenance.
The cumulative cash and NPV exclude equity/debt funding injections and cash interest. Peak funding must be provided; the1% real discount rate is a required-return scenario, not an offered loan.
These orders are alternatives to earlier array construction procurement. Recurring mature renewal demand is a different time phase, not additional orders in this campaign.

A pressure/launch/processing design must preserve the assumed delivered costs throughout the campaign. Early low-pressure advantages do not establish the assumed10% or25% whole-production cost reductions.
